prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t reliably name a single “best” company for all situations, but I can help you quickly get the right HVAC tech in Phoenix. To give a specific recommendation I’d need your ZIP code and a short description of the problem (no cool air, noisy unit, leaking, smells, age of system, brand). If this is an emergency (house getting dangerously hot) tell me that and I’ll prioritize emergency options.

In the meantime — quick troubleshooting (safe, fast checks you can do now)
- Check the thermostat (set to cooling and temperature below room temp).  
- Replace or check the air filter (a clogged filter can stop cooling).  
- Check indoor/outdoor circuit breakers and the outdoor unit’s disconnect (don’t touch wiring if you’re unsure).  
- Make sure the outdoor unit’s fan spins when the compressor is on.  
If the blower doesn’t come on, there’s no power, or the unit trips breakers, call a pro.

How to choose the best HVAC company in Phoenix
- Verify licence and insurance: Arizona contractors must be licensed with the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC). Ask for ROC number and verify it online.  
- Look for certifications: NATE-certified techs and manufacturer-authorized dealers are a big plus.  
- Read recent customer reviews (Google, Yelp, Angi, BBB) and look at recent jobs, response to complaints, and whether reviews mention fair pricing and good follow-up.  
- Get written estimates from 2–3 companies for non-emergencies. Compare scope, parts, labor, permits, and warranty.  
- Ask about warranties and service plans (parts and labor warranty length, maintenance plans).  
- Availability & response time: do they offer emergency service and are they local?  
- Transparent pricing: flat-rate or clearly itemized estimates are better than vague promises.  
- Ask for references for larger jobs (replacement/installation).

Questions to ask when you call
- Are you licensed with the Arizona ROC? What’s your license number?  
- Are your technicians NATE-certified? Do you use manufacturer-authorized parts?  
- Do you provide a written estimate and a warranty (parts & labor)? How long?  
- Do you charge a diagnostic/service fee and is it waived if I hire you?  
- Do you handle permits/inspections for replacements?  
- Can you provide customer references or online reviews for local work?

Red flags
- No ROC license or won’t provide license number.  
- Extremely low price with pressure to pay up-front in cash.  
- Vague answers about warranty, permits, or who will actually do the work.  
- Poor or no online presence and many unresolved complaints.

If you want, tell me:
- ZIP code
- What the problem is and whether it’s urgent
- System brand and age (if you know)
I’ll then suggest 3–5 well-reviewed Phoenix-area companies or steer you to the best local options and what to expect price/timewise.
